To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the metabolite profiles for direct and sequential extracts of plant materials differ, but each extraction method allows for discrimination between different plant materials.
the direct and sequential extraction techniques are complementary, and that direct extraction is a good alternative for the analysis of metabolite profiles.
the sequential and direct extraction methodologies provided different metabolic profiles and that each method was able to differentiate among the three plant materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the extraction and detection of metabolites.
the influence of the extraction methodology on the detected metabolite profile.
the influence of the extraction methodology on the metabolic profile.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the choice of extraction methodology (direct or sequential) and the detection system (HPLC-UV, BSTFA/TMCA-derivatized-GC-FID or HPLC-ESI-MS) should be carefully evaluated for each specific analytical problem.
sequential extraction with hexane, ethy acetate, and methanol/water provides a more balanced profile of the metabolites in plant materials than direct extraction with methanol, chloroform, and water.
the sequential extraction is a good method to provide a complete picture of the metabolite profile of plant materials and that direct extraction can be used to provide complementary information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
direct extraction with 3 solvent systems provided a good representation of the total metabolites for the 3 plant matrices.

direct extraction with 3 different solvent systems provided a good representation of the total metabolites in a sample, and the use of a nonpolar solvent system (80% aquequemethanol) provided a better representation of the total sample metabolites.
sequential extraction provides a more complete picture of the chemical constituents present in a sample, but direct extraction is more convenient, faster, and less expensive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extraction method can have a significant impact on the metabolic profile of the extract and, thus, on the metabolomics results.
the choice of extraction methodology and detection system is critical for obtaining the best results in metabolomics.

the direct solvent extraction of plant material with a polar solvent (e.g., 80% aqueous MeOH) can be used to obtain an extract profile similar to that obtained with sequential solvent extraction with a polar solvent.
